text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Lower Saxony premier Gerhard Schroeder of the opposition Social Democrats presents himself as campaigner against crime. Greens, potential coalition partners, dismiss his crusade

- Parliamentary whip for the opposition Social Democrats Franz Muentefering says party will say whether it will form a coalition by SPD party congress in mid April 1998. He said his party was considering a coalition with the environmental Greens as an option
- German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel says Germany pays too much in EU constributions and demands a fairer system.
HANDELSBLATT

- Hans Olaf Henkel, president of the BDI German Industry Federation, says Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition should stick to what is politically possible and that a reduction in company tax should take top priority
- President of the Federal Labour Office Bernhard Jagoda says unemployment could be halved by the year 2002. He expects an improvement in joblessness this year and particularly in 1998
- Chairman of the DGB trades union federation Dieter Schulte distanced himself from IG Metall metalworkers' union leader and his campaign against Chancellor Helmut Kohl
- Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel and Bavaria premier urge reduction in Germany's EU contributions
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG

- Head of Free Democrats (FDP), Chancellor Helmut Kohl's junior coalition partners, Wolfgang Gerhardt called on Kohl's CDU/CSU for more courage to push through reforms despite opposition Social Democrat blocade in upper house of parliament
- Money launderers will be treated like drug traders by the Federal Court of Justice, Germany's highest criminal court
- German Farms Minister Jochen Borchert announces resistance to Brussels agricultural reform, fearing huge income cuts for German farmers
- Cartel Office is sceptical about pay television station TV-Allianz set up by Bertelsmann and Leo Kirch
DIE WELT

- Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats and Bavarian sister party the Christian Social Union along with opposition Social Democrats want to make fight against crime chief election campaign theme.
- Serious floods in eastern Germany along river Oder and and with constant rain
- Worldwide breakdown on the Internet. Many millions of business documents and E-mails are jammed.
